checked: Amodei's essay 'We Must Pace the Frontier' (Sep 12) proposes three steps: embedded evaluators with employee-like access (METR named as an example), democratic coordination on common safety standards, and global coordination with authoritarian governments across four levels (L1 prohibit narrow dangerous uses such as bioweapons, L2 both sides test models for acute risks, L3 limit recursive self-improvement rates, L4 full pacing or pause). It warns that 'in 6-12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet' with 'hundreds of billions of dollars in damage'. Altman agreed on X and said OpenAI would do the same on evaluators; Musk posted 'Dario is right'; Nadella said Microsoft welcomes 'the research, focus, and deliberate pacing needed to get alignment right'. Chamath wrote that Dario 'makes the case to stop open source and concentrate enormous technological and economic power with Anthropic'; Sacks asked why AI companies need Washington's permission to slow down.
corrections: Nadella's full quote is 'the research, focus, and deliberate pacing needed to get alignment right' (Sep 13); the MAI Code of Conduct was published Sep 14 as a draft for public consultation, not alongside the statement. Sacks's point (Sep 14) was that companies do not need government permission to slow down, slightly different from 'voluntary commitments make regulation unnecessary'. Level 4 is a full pacing or pause, 'general slowdown' is fine.
